title: Make Quick Veggie Spring Rolls Using a Mandoline
meta_description: Easily make restaurant-quality veggie spring rolls at home using a mandoline for precise veggie slices.
html:
When it comes to delicious and versatile appetizers or snacks, few options beat the classic veggie spring roll. By using a Mandoline Slicer and some basic ingredients, you can recreate your favorite takeout dishes or experiment with new flavors.

Choosing the Right Veggies for Veggie Spring Rolls

The beauty of veggie spring rolls lies in their ability to incorporate a wide array of colorful vegetables. For this recipe, we'll focus on a few popular options that work well together: shredded carrots, sliced cabbage, diced bell peppers, and shredded beets. You can also experiment with other ingredients like shredded zucchini, diced cucumbers, or sliced mushrooms.

When selecting your veggies, choose ones that will hold their shape after being sliced and assembled into the spring roll. Crunchy veggies like carrots and cabbage are ideal, while softer veggies like cucumbers may require some extra care when handling.

Preparing Veggies with a Mandoline

To achieve uniform, restaurant-thin slices, a Mandoline Slicer is a must-have tool. This versatile kitchen gadget allows you to slice a variety of vegetables with precision and speed. For this recipe, use the Mandoline Slicer to slice the carrots and cabbage into thin strips, and the beets into uniform discs.

Remember to always use the hand guard when slicing to prevent accidents and injuries. The adjustable blade also ensures you can achieve the perfect slice thickness for your specific veggie.

Assembling Veggie Spring Rolls

Now that you have your sliced veggies, it's time to assemble the spring rolls. Lay a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface and place a small handful of the sliced veggies in the center. Brush the edges with a little water to help the wrapper stick together during assembly.

Next, add any additional ingredients you like, such as chopped herbs or a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Finally, fold the bottom half of the wrapper up over the filling, followed by the sides and the top half. Press the edges together to seal the roll.

Additional Tips and Variations

For an extra crispy exterior, try dipping the assembled spring rolls in a mixture of equal parts cornstarch and water before frying. Alternatively, bake the spring rolls in a preheated oven at 400°F (200°C) for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown.

  • Experiment with different seasonings, such as soy sauce or oyster sauce, to give your spring rolls an added depth of flavor.
  • For a vegetarian or vegan option, replace the traditional egg-based wrapper with a rice paper or cornstarch-based alternative.
  • Don't be afraid to get creative with your filling ingredients – the possibilities are endless!

FAQ

Q: What's the best way to store assembled spring rolls before frying or baking?

A: Store assembled spring rolls in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Before frying or baking, bring the rolls to room temperature to ensure even cooking.

Q: Can I use pre-shredded veggies for the spring roll filling?

A: While pre-shredded veggies are convenient, they may not hold their shape as well as freshly sliced veggies. For the best results, use the Mandoline Slicer to slice your veggies just before assembling the spring rolls.

Q: How do I prevent the spring rolls from falling apart during frying or baking?

A: To prevent the spring rolls from falling apart, make sure to seal the edges tightly during assembly and use a gentle touch when handling the rolls. If they do break apart, simply reassemble them and proceed with cooking.
